newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P raises Nordbanken outlook to positive.
newsitem.headline: S&P raises Nordbanken outlook to positive.

text.p: Credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it revised the outlook on Swedish state-controlled bank Nordbanken AB's long-term ratings to positive from stable.
S&P said in a statement it affirmed the bank's single A senior unsecured debt ratings, its A/A-1 counterparty rating and its A-1 commercial paper ratings.
It also affirmed its A-1 U.S. commercial paper rating of Nordbanken N.A. Inc which is guaranteed by Nordbanken.
S&P also affirmed its single A- counterparty rating of Industrikredit AB.
S&P said the bank was Sweden's fourth largest with total assets of 368 billion crowns.

"Nordbanken's ratings reflect the bank's strong market position in the Swedish retail banking market, solid funding base, robust capitalisation, improved asset quality and good income-generatnig capacity," S&P said.
It said the bank had recovered markedly from problems of the early 1990s, when the government had to provide substantial financial support.
S&P said Nordbanken was well-placed to meet its competition, which will continue to pressure the Swedish banking sector.

"Although profitability throughout the sector is not expected to reach the high level attained in 1996, the measures that Nordbanken has taken will help the group's efficiency and contribute to the bank's ability to achieve a stable performance over the medium term," S&P said.
